rules.title: Abstraction Placement
rules.rule: Introduce abstractions wherever genuinely justified and nowhere else; first inspect existing owners and simpler alternatives.

examples.description: Creating a new registry for a responsibility already owned by the current registry.
examples.lesson: Duplication is not an abstraction improvement.

test.instruction: Review each touched artifact and immediate contracts. Identify justified and unjustified abstractions, alternatives already available, and exact evidence. Report pass, fail, not_applicable or inconclusive per rule.

rules.title: Extreme KISS Simplicity
rules.rule: If a solution is not super-simple, it is totally wrong. Avoid complex wrapper abstractions and bypasses when native platform and existing contracts exist.

examples.description: Adding intermediate caching layers or shadow stores when the direct store already owns persistence.

test.instruction: Verify that the implementation chooses the simplest correct expression without unnecessary layers.

rules.title: Single Responsibility & Tightness
rules.rule: Every touched artifact must earn its existence with one clear owner and responsibility. Tighten statements and remove redundant branches or obsolete workarounds.

examples.description: Placing domain operations in their owning domain tool module rather than scattering across general utilities.

test.instruction: Assess whether touched methods have scattered or fragmented responsibilities.
